entries.title: The Shepherd Who Looks After Me
entries.text:
Yahweh is the shepherd who looks after me.
I will never lack anything.
entries.reflection:
A shepherd stays close to the sheep. He watches the path, the weather, and where the grass and water are. The sheep don't have to figure all of that out alone. Psalm 23 begins with that picture. Yahweh is the shepherd who looks after me.

The next line says, "I will never lack anything." A good shepherd sees to what the sheep need: a path, something to eat, a watchful eye. Wants and needs aren't always the same thing. Some days still feel short, short on time, or money, or peace. Those days are real. This verse sets them inside a larger care. You are looked after. Your life is shared with a shepherd who walks the road with you.

So today you can ask for what you need. You can also notice what has already been given, even if it's only a meal and a place to sit down. The shepherd is already on this road with you. You can walk it as someone who is known and kept.
entries.prayer: Yahweh, my shepherd, look after me today. You see what I need, even the things I haven't said out loud. Lead me and keep me close. Give me a quiet heart that can rest in your care, and thank you for walking this road with me. Amen.

entries.title: A Hiding Place and Strength
entries.text:
God is our hiding place and our strength,
always ready to help in trouble.
entries.reflection:
Trouble isn't a surprise in this verse. It's part of the road, and God meets us there. He is our hiding place and our strength, always ready to help.

A hiding place is where you can catch your breath and admit you're afraid. Strength is what helps you stand up again and take the next step. God is both at once. "Always ready" means his help doesn't make you wait until you've calmed down. You can turn to him while your hands are still shaking, sitting in the car before you go inside.

Hiding here isn't disappearing from the people who need you. It's how you find your feet again. Rest long enough to stand, then go back to the work and the people in front of you. When a hard day comes, you can start with a simple prayer: be my shelter, and be my strength. He is already ready to help.
entries.prayer: God, you are my hiding place and my strength. I'm bringing you the trouble I'm carrying. Shelter me, and give me strength for what's in front of me. Thank you that you are already ready to help. Amen.

entries.title: Where You Put Your Weight
entries.text:
Trust Yahweh completely.
Do not lean on what you understand yourself.
entries.reflection:
"Trust Yahweh completely." Then the proverb tells you where not to put all your weight. Your own understanding is too small to carry everything.

This book also spends line after line teaching people to pay attention, to learn, and to choose with care. A mind that thinks is a gift. Trust and careful thought belong together. The warning is about leaning. When you lean, you rest your full weight on something. If the only thing holding you up is your own view of a situation, that view will sometimes be too thin. You can't see the end of a choice from the middle of it. You can't see what a year will ask of you.

To trust Yahweh is to include him in the choice, and to let his wisdom carry what yours cannot. Pray before you decide, even if the prayer is short and said at a red light. Ask for a clear mind and a humble one. Then act, with open hands, even while some questions are still unanswered.
entries.prayer: Yahweh, I trust you with this whole day. Give me a clear mind and a humble one. Guide the choice in front of me, and teach me to include you in it. I place what I cannot see into your hands. Amen.

entries.title: Brave While You Wait
entries.text:
Wait for Yahweh.
Be strong and brave in your heart.
Yes, wait for Yahweh.
entries.reflection:
"Wait for Yahweh." The psalm says it twice, with a charge in the middle: be strong and brave in your heart. Waiting and bravery are set side by side. This kind of waiting isn't doing nothing on the couch. It's a steady heart turned toward God while an answer is still on the way.

Most of us would rather hold the answer than hold the wait. We fill the quiet with worry, or we shove on a door because the right one hasn't opened yet. The psalm calls the heart back. The strength it names sits in the place where fear talks the loudest. Bravery there can look quiet from the outside. It can look like telling God the truth, keeping a promise you already made, or staying soft on a day when the way through is still hidden.

Yes, wait for Yahweh. He is worth waiting for. The thing you placed in his hands is still in his hands.
entries.prayer: Yahweh, I'm waiting for you, and the wait is hard. Make my heart strong and brave while I wait. Keep me steady and honest. I place this hope in your hands again. Help me wait for you. Amen.

entries.title: The God Who Does Not Get Tired
entries.text:
Do you not know? Have you not heard?
Yahweh is the everlasting God,
the Creator of the ends of the earth.
He does not get tired or worn out.
No one can measure his understanding.
entries.reflection:
Isaiah asks a question that works like a hand on your shoulder: Do you not know? Have you not heard? It's easy to forget the answer on a day when you're worn out. Yahweh is the everlasting God, the Creator of the ends of the earth. He does not get tired or worn out. No one can measure his understanding.

Set that next to a long evening, when the dishes are still in the sink and your mind is done. We run out of strength. He does not. The verse meets us in that weariness and tells us who is still strong.

Everlasting means he has no beginning and no end. Creator of the ends of the earth means the far places you'll never see are his, and so is the room where you're sitting. His understanding is wider than anything we can measure. That's a gift when your own thoughts have run out of road. You can bring him a problem you can't sort out. You can also bring him nothing but your tiredness. He is still listening, and he is not worn out.
entries.prayer: Everlasting God, you made the ends of the earth, and you never grow tired. I'm worn out, and I have questions I can't measure. Stay with me. Give me the strength I need for today. Amen.

entries.title: Faithful and Present
entries.text: Nobody will withstand you as long as you live. I stood by Moses, and I will stand by you in the same way. You will find me faithful and present; I will not leave you.
entries.reflection:
These words were spoken to Joshua as he took up the work Moses had carried. God says he stood by Moses, and he will stand by Joshua in the same way. "You will find me faithful and present; I will not leave you."

Joshua had a heavy task in front of him, the kind that can keep you up at night. God doesn't first hand him a longer list. He speaks to that weight with a promise about his own character. He is faithful. He is present. He stays with the person he sends, and he doesn't walk off once the work gets hard.

Our days aren't Joshua's days, and our work is our own. What we can hold from this verse is the way God stays. When something in front of you feels too big, you can ask for that same company. Tell him you need him to be faithful and present right here, in this room, with this task. Then take the step that's in front of you, with him beside you.
entries.prayer: Yahweh, you are faithful and present. You stood with your servants, and you stay with them. This in front of me feels too big. Be with me in it, and help me take the next step with you beside me. Amen.

entries.title: Close to the Brokenhearted
entries.text:
Yahweh is close to people with broken hearts.
He rescues those whose spirits are crushed.
entries.reflection:
Some pain makes a person feel far from everyone, and far from God as well. Psalm 34 says Yahweh is close to people with broken hearts. He rescues those whose spirits are crushed.

Close means near. God comes close to the person who is hurting. In this verse, a broken heart is a place he moves toward, not a place he avoids. Crushed is an honest word too. The psalm lets the hurt stay as large as it is. God comes anyway.

Rescue is his real help. Some losses are still losses this afternoon, and the ache may still be there when you try to sleep. His rescue means you are met inside that hurt by someone who can actually help. You can tell him the true size of it, without cleaning it up first. Sit with this verse if your spirit feels crushed: he is close, and he rescues.
entries.prayer: Yahweh, you are close to people with broken hearts. Please come near to me. You know the true size of this hurt. Rescue me, and stay close so I can tell you're here. Amen.
